reason: E1 describes coherent precipitates enhancing ductility in a W-based refractory HEA, but it concerns an fcc matrix and SCCP process, not the bcc WTaTiVZr alloy or plasma-facing temperatures. E2 reports multiple phases including Laves and TiC in WTaTiVCr alloys sintered at 1600 °C, but does not show nanoscale coherent precipitates improving ductility. Neither passage supports the specific claim that WTaTiVZr will form beneficial coherent precipitates at 1300–1500 °C.
premises: Nanoscale coherent precipitates can form in refractory HEAs under high-temperature exposure
Coherent precipitates enhance ductility and toughness by accommodating dislocations and deflecting cracks
The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy can develop such precipitates at 1300–1500 °C
The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates this mechanism in W-based refractory HEAs
